title: I must, the car
summary: je dois / tu dois = I must / you must. It literally means 'I owe', so it also works for money: tu dois trente euros. You learn réparer, préparer, comparer, la voiture and la machine, and why a final e makes you pronounce the consonant before it.
points: je dois (I must / I have to / I owe) is related to 'debt'. The s is silent.
A consonant followed by a final e IS pronounced: la porte, trente, la machine. Without the e it's usually silent.
Spot building blocks like ré- / re- and swap them: réparer, préparer, comparer.
Take your time: pause the track and build each sentence one piece at a time.

vocab.en: I must / you must (also: I owe / you owe)

drills.en: I have to repair something later.
drills.fr: Je dois réparer quelque chose plus tard.

drills.en: You have to repair the door.
I have to repair the car.
Can you repair the car a little later?
drills.fr: Peux-tu réparer la voiture un peu plus tard ?
